device.description: Dual 16-bit voltage-output DAC with 24-bit SPI-compatible write-only interface, per-channel data buffers and software load bits
device.note: dac8532.pdf (SBAS246B) p.3 pin functions, p.5 power requirements (VDD 2.7-5.5 V) and logic inputs, p.6 timing requirements and Figure 1, p.14 power-on reset, input shift register (Figure 33) and SYNC interrupt, p.15 power-down modes (Table 1), p.16 control matrix (Table 2) and power-down commands (Table 3), p.16-17 operation examples

protocol.note: 24-bit word: DB23-DB22 reserved 0, DB21 LDB, DB20 LDA, DB19 don't care, DB18 buffer select (0 = A, 1 = B), DB17-DB16 PD1/PD0, DB15-DB0 data (Table 2); executed on the 24th SCLK falling edge, SYNC high earlier discards the word

pages: p.3 (pins), p.5 (power requirements, logic inputs), p.6 (timing, Figure 1), p.14 (power-on reset, input shift register, SYNC interrupt), p.15 (power-down, Table 1), p.16-17 (control matrix Table 2, power-down commands Table 3, operation examples)
notModeled: analog outputs and the shared VREF reference (never driven)

power-down: the PD1/PD0 command goes into the data buffer and takes effect when that channel is loaded; the model stores it in PWR at once (a later data write to the buffer sets it back to 00), and the buffer's data are kept
power-down exit time (2.5 us at 5 V, 5 us at 3 V) and output settling
SCLK frequency (20 MHz below VDD 3.6 V, 30 MHz above) and setup/hold limits t1-t9
words with DB23/DB22 not 0 are ignored (the datasheet requires 0)
SPI mode: data taken on SCLK falling edges with SCLK high at SYNC fall (Figure 1); modeled as mode 2
no read-back: the interface is write-only
